public_task_requirement: Please implement a website for a credit repair company to generate leads. The website should have a form-filling function, allowing users to input personal information and credit status. The website should also have a credit score inquiry function and an introduction to credit repair services. Users can browse the website, learn about credit repair services, and fill out the form to submit lead information. Set old lace as the body background and use rosy brown for the UI.

task_summary.requirement_coverage: The site targeted a credit repair lead-generation landing page with three core user-facing capabilities: a form for personal/credit-status lead capture, a credit score inquiry action, and an introduction to credit repair services, all styled with an old lace body background and rosy brown UI. Verified strengths: the credit score inquiry flow was observed to work and display a score/feedback; the color palette was judged to match the requested scheme; the page rendered without visible runtime errors. Main functional risks: the lead form was not confirmed as submitted before interaction budget exhaustion, so the confirmation state was not reached; the services/introduction content was not fully verified and was reported as not found in the interaction trace; navigation/content visibility depended on switching views, which limited confirmation of the required landing-page coverage. Visible observations: the homepage showed navigation buttons, a credit score CTA, and a lead form view existed in the implementation, but the evaluator’s screenshot-based review noted that the first screen did not visibly present all required sections together.
verified_strengths: Credit score inquiry was confirmed to display a score and qualitative feedback after the inquiry button was used.
The requested old lace background and rosy brown UI styling were observed as matching the specification.
The page rendered cleanly with no visible errors in the evaluation evidence.
primary_functional_risks: Form submission was not reached, so the lead-recording confirmation state remains unverified.
The credit repair services introduction was not confirmed during interaction and was reported as absent/not found in the evaluated flow.
Because the site uses separate views, required content may not be visible until navigation occurs, increasing the risk that the landing experience does not satisfy the lead-gen brief immediately.
primary_visual_observations: The landing page showed navigation and a credit score CTA, but the screenshot-based review said the form-filling function and detailed services introduction were not visibly present on the first screen.
The color scheme was observed as compliant, but the text contrast on the hero area was noted as low in the appearance evaluator output.

appearance_reflection.observed_result: The home view renders the heading "Welcome to Credit Repair Experts" inside a white card, while the page background is set to oldlace and the navigation bar and buttons use rosybrown. The reviewer reported that the heading text contrast against the background is very low, and that the typography is minimal with room for stronger font weight or contrast. The code also sets the global body text color to rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.87) in :root, which can further reduce readability on light surfaces.
appearance_reflection.likely_cause_or_limitation: Appearance issue supported by the screenshot review: the text is present but not readable enough on the first screen, so the fix is to make the heading and body text stand out more against the background.
appearance_reflection.preventative_action: Use a text color and font weight combination that keeps the main heading and body copy clearly readable against the page background. Verify on the first screen that the primary heading and introductory text remain legible without relying on scrolling or zoom.
appearance_reflection.verification: Render the landing page and confirm the main heading and body text are readable at normal size on the initial screen, with sufficient contrast against the background and surrounding UI blocks.
appearance_reflection.transfer_limits: Applies to landing pages and lead-generation sites that use light backgrounds with colored UI panels or buttons.

functional_reflections.user_trigger: After entering valid personal information and credit status in the lead form, the user submits the form.
functional_reflections.expected_state_change: The page replaces the form with a visible confirmation message indicating the lead information was received.
functional_reflections.observed_result: The tester filled in the form fields and selected a credit issue, but did not click the submit button, so no confirmation message appeared.
functional_reflections.likely_cause_or_limitation: (unverified against code) The check stopped before the final submit action because the interaction budget was exhausted; the form submission state was therefore never triggered.
functional_reflections.preventative_action: For any form that ends with a confirmation state, keep the submit button visible and reachable after all required fields are filled, and ensure the confirmation is rendered immediately when the form submit event fires.

investigation.task: The check asked whether a user can fill out the lead form with personal information and credit status and then submit it to receive a confirmation message. The tester’s final answer was PARTIAL because the form was filled but the submit button was never clicked.
investigation.reached_target: The tester did reach the form feature on the site and entered data into the personal-information fields and the credit-issue dropdown area, so the target feature was exercised. The run stopped before the final submit action due to interaction budget exhaustion, not because of a page error.
investigation.screenshots: The screenshots show the lead form page with John, Doe, john.doe@example.com, and 1234567890 already entered, and the credit issue select still visible. No confirmation/success message is shown, which matches the tester’s note that submission had not yet happened.
investigation.code_path: The feature exists in src/views/FormView.vue and is reachable from App.vue via the Get Started button. The form component includes a submit handler that sets submitted = true and conditionally swaps the form for a success message, so the intended confirmation state is present in code; the check did not reach that state.
investigation.candidates: 1) Unexercised final step / interaction budget exhaustion: supported by the tester’s own final answer saying the submit button was never clicked. 2) Missing or broken submit confirmation: ruled out by the code path in FormView.vue, which defines submitForm() and a v-if success section. 3) Unreadable styling: ruled out because the screenshots clearly show the form fields and labels, not a hidden or illegible confirmation state.
investigation.conclusion: The only established cause is that the tester ran out of interactions before clicking the submit button, so the confirmation state was never reached.
investigation.preventative_action: For any lead form, keep the submit control reachable in the same interaction flow as the fields and make the post-submit confirmation appear immediately after the form state changes, so a user can complete the flow without needing extra navigation or hidden steps.
investigation.verification: After entering valid lead details, click the form’s submit button and verify that the form is replaced by a visible confirmation message.
investigation.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to single-page lead forms that require an explicit submit action before showing confirmation; it does not address unrelated navigation, styling, or other site sections.
